summary: All four real-data experiments and solver checks ran on CPU. Method and house/Senate/Chicago direction-of-effect claims are reproduced; mesothelioma is partially reproduced because the held-out error is tied with the common model on this split.

claims.observation: Four-block implementation runs to residual-based stopping, and matrix-free product-grid matvec agrees with an explicit Cartesian-product Laplacian on the tested graph.
claims.notes: The large Chicago Laplacian is applied as a Kronecker/product operator to keep memory bounded; this is algebraically equivalent to the product graph.

claims.observation: The stratified model reaches test ANLL 0.630 versus 0.749 separate and 0.730 common, but test error is 0.303 for both stratified and common rather than the paper's 0.27 and 0.30.
claims.notes: The supplied UCI workbook and deterministic seed are used; the paper's single random split and older feature-processing stack are not fully recoverable from the PDF.

claims.observation: Stratified test RMSE is 0.1813, common is 0.3156, separate is 1.5379, and the 50-tree random forest is 0.1832, matching the paper's ordering and reported values.
claims.notes: The filtered 21,596-row asset produces the paper's 16,197/5,399 train/test counts.

claims.observation: Stratified test ANLL is 0.538 versus 0.693 separate and 0.703 common, preserving the paper's improvement direction and approximately its 0.61/0.70 reference values.
claims.notes: The current MEDSL file is filtered to 1976-2016 and statewide general-election winners; the state-border adjacency is documented in provenance.

claims.observation: On all 3,494,400 cells, stratified test ANLL is 0.2445 versus 0.7389 separate and 0.2783 common; the model uses the paper-scale product graph and improves over both baselines.
claims.notes: The run completed on CPU in 186.6 seconds at the configured 80 iterations; further iterations can be requested with --maxiter for tighter residual tolerance.
